[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The cirrhosis-matched L1 gold record for meptazinol reports absolute F = 27.9 ± 5.3% in cirrhotic patients after 200 mg p.o. versus 25 mg i.v., reproduced in L2 records C30 and C43; this direct cirrhosis-context endpoint is above the 20% threshold.

All other L1 gold-context records report F values at or above 20% (cilomilast 96%, vernakalant 58–71%, irbesartan about 60–82%, imipramine 43.6%, ranolazine 35–50%, urapidil 72%, anlotinib 41–77%, ONO-4641 0.710), so the calibrated gold context does not support a low prediction.

L5 verapamil-scaffold records show high intestinal permeability and near-complete absorption, with P-gp efflux present but not limiting absorption; this supports that the verapamil-like backbone can be absorbed.

L6 verapamil hepatic-clearance records show high intrinsic clearance and short metabolic half-life in human liver microsomes/hepatocytes, indicating extensive first-pass metabolism for verapamil; however, these records are for verapamil, not the query, and were generated in non-cirrhotic systems, so they do not affirmatively establish F < 20% for the query under cirrhosis.

The query's cyclic bis-sulfone modification is untested in all supplied records; transfer from verapamil is indirect, and the cirrhosis condition may reduce first-pass metabolism, so the high prediction is retained with low confidence.

evidence_gaps: No query-specific absolute oral bioavailability or matched oral-versus-IV AUC/Cmax data are available.
No query-specific pharmacokinetic data under cirrhosis are available; meptazinol is the only cirrhosis-matched L1 context.
No query-specific hepatic clearance or metabolic-stability data are available; L6 records are for verapamil and analogs.
The effect of the query's cyclic bis-sulfone modification on permeability, P-gp efflux, and CYP3A4 metabolism is untested.
Cirrhosis may alter first-pass metabolism, but the direction and magnitude for the query are unknown.
No query-specific solubility or permeability data are available.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F >= 20%) because the most direct cirrhosis-context gold record (meptazinol F 27.9%) and all other L1 gold contexts are at or above threshold; L5 verapamil-scaffold records show high intestinal absorption and efflux not limiting. L6 verapamil hepatic-clearance records indicate extensive first-pass metabolism for verapamil, but they are not query-specific and were obtained in non-cirrhotic systems, so they do not affirmatively establish F < 20% for the query under cirrhosis. Confidence remains low due to absence of query-specific PK.

You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.
